samples.summary: Painted-pixel read-back (`cellsOf`) is lossy: it ignores rect height and snaps any x/y to the nearest grid line, so geometrically wrong highlights can still read as correct
samples.evidence: `cellsOf` destructures only `[x, y, w]` — the rect height is never inspected — and `nearest()` maps *any* y to the closest entry of `rowY` (it always returns some index, with no tolerance check). A selection band painted at the wrong height (e.g. half a row tall, or spanning two rows), or offset by a large but sub-half-row amount, still yields the same `row,col` labels, so the tests' claim to be "measured on painted pixels" is weaker than stated: they verify the set of (x,w) bands per nearest row, not the rectangle a user sees. The assertions are still non-vacuous for the column/merge behaviour of #1049; the gap is in vertical geometry precision.

samples.summary: The nested-table fix is only covered at the `normalizeRange` unit level; no test asserts the nested table's cell-range highlight is actually painted correctly
samples.evidence: The diff's stated user-visible symptom is that "the columns a merge covers then painted only inside the merged row". The only new coverage for the nested branch is `cell-range-expand.test.ts:161` ('expands inside a nested table too'), which asserts the normalized `tableCellRange` indices only. The new painted-pixel suite (`table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts`) uses `doc.insertTable` at top level, so `resolveNestedTableLayout(...)?.dataBlock.tableData` is never the branch taken there, and `buildCellRangeRects` for a nested table is never exercised end-to-end. Grepping `buildCellRangeRects|resolveNestedTableLayout` across packages/docs returns only src files plus `cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts` and `copy-integrity.test.ts`, neither of which asserts nested cell-range highlight geometry. The unit test does fail pre-fix (pre-fix `table` is undefined, so `normalizeCellRange` returns end colIndex 0 instead of 1), so this is narrowness rather than fake coverage.

samples.summary: Only one shift+click scenario is tested for the new branch; sibling cases (shift+click landing on a covered cell, shift+click back toward the anchor, shift+click in a nested table) have no coverage
samples.evidence: The new `else if (anchorCellInfo && anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId === pos.blockId)` branch is exercised by exactly one test — `table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts:283` ('shift+click on a cell in another row…'), a downward (0,1)→(2,1) gesture. Untested variants of the same new code: a shift+click whose target point falls inside a merged/covered cell (the branch takes `end: cellAddr` and `focus: cell.blocks[0].id` without a merge-owner resolution step that the drag path has at text-editor.ts:2385-2407), a backwards shift+click, and a repeat shift+click that should re-extend from the same raw anchor. Searched: grep `shiftKey` across packages/docs/test (11 files; only the new file touches table cell ranges) and grep `anchorCellInfo` in src.

samples.summary: Six of the eight new tests cover the pre-existing drag path, not code this diff changes
samples.evidence: The drag tests at lines 259-281 and 301 all go through `TextEditor`'s mousemove drag handling (text-editor.ts:2352-2456), which this diff does not touch; only the shift+click test at line 283 exercises the new text-editor branch (2084-2103), and none of them exercise the selection.ts nested-table fallback (they use a top-level table). They are useful regression coverage, but the suite's framing as "the cell-rectangle contract of #1049" overstates how much of the *change* they pin down.
